AdjustLoyaltyPointsRequest.description: **A correction is a new entry, never an edit.** Reversing an entry writes a row pointing at it through `reversedLoyaltyPointsId`; granting goodwill writes a row with no reversal target. Either way the movement has a reason and an author, and the history stays walkable.

points.description: Signed. Negative removes points, and the balance may not go below zero.

reason.description: **Goodwill, correction or expiry reversal, and nothing else (decided 28 September, audit R149).** A service-recovery grant is `goodwill`, a fraud or migration fix is `correction`, and returning points that expired in error is `expiryReversal`. None of them moves the tier or `lifetimePoints`.

reversedLoyaltyPointsId.description: The entry this reverses, when it is a reversal. **Set it and the sign is checked against the original** — a reversal that does not cancel what it names is a second grant wearing a correction's label.

ConsentPurpose.description: `storedPaymentCredential` (a card saved for later, `storePaymentToken`) and `facePassEnrolment` (a face enrolled for entry, `enrolFacePass`) are purposes of their own (R8 blocker ORDERS-MONEY-C21, CHG-R8MIG-022), so a screen picks the row by its purpose instead of guessing: each tenant has one `marketing.consent_purpose` row of each, seeded with the tenant's other purposes.

orderId.description: The order whose checkout carried the opt-in (source `checkout`, M18-15): the UUIDv7 of orders.sales_order. Null for every other source.

verifiedContactRef.description: The verified contact the checkout opt-in was given against (ADR-0045), as the keyed hash the guest match policy uses; never the raw address. It is how a checkout consent given without an account is attached to the profile when the contact later matches one.

requiresRenewal.description: True where the notice has been superseded since consent was given.

ruleGroups.description: **Nested AND / OR / NOT groups** (contract gap CHG-WIR-007, BO-755; CHG-CSA-045). Where present, the segment matches `criteria` (combined by `match`) AND every group here. Absent keeps the flat list.

effectiveFrom.description: The segment is evaluated for sends only from this time.

ownerPrincipalId.description: Who answers for the segment; defaults to its creator.

requiresApproval.description: Where true, a campaign may use the segment only after an `approvals` request on it is approved.

Customer360ServiceProfileView.x-ticvai-persistence: none — projection over marketing.guest_profile, pii.subject, pii.subject_contact, marketing.loyalty_position, marketing.guest_preference, marketing.consent_record, marketing.suppression, marketing.case, orders.sales_order, orders.reservation, orders.group_booking, access.entitlement and wallet.balance
Customer360ServiceProfileView.description: The service view of one guest. Fields the caller may not see are null, never omitted.

customerName.description: Null unless the caller holds GUEST_VIEW_PII.

contactDetails.description: Masked (e.g. `j***@example.com`, `+971 ** *** 4821`) unless the caller holds GUEST_VIEW_PII.

customerValue.description: Lifetime net spend across the tenant.

riskAttentionIndicator.description: `attention` with an open complaint or an unresolved refund case; `risk` with a breached SLA or a repeat contact on the same issue.

accessibilityRequirements.description: Null unless the caller holds GUEST_VIEW_PII.

communicationRestrictions.description: Channels the guest must not be contacted on (`getSuppressionList`).

aiSummary.description: Where the AI policy enables `summarise`. AI-derived and labelled as such.

GuestAttributeModel.description: Board 1.3. **Visibility by jurisdiction is what makes this a model and not a form.**

lawfulInJurisdictions.description: **Empty means everywhere.** A nationality field lawful in one jurisdiction and not another cannot be a column somebody ships.

GuestExtraFieldDefinition.x-ticvai-persistence: none — composed from a field and its options
GuestExtraFieldDefinition.description: **A select with no options is not a field**, so the options come back with the definition rather than from a second call.

GuestIntelligence.description: Board 1.10. **Explainable, or an agent will ignore it or over-trust it.**

limitations.description: **Policy and data limitations travel with the score**, so the rule that prediction never overrides consent cannot be forgotten downstream.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

subjectId.description:
Opaque reference. Personal data lives in the separately erasable store, which is what makes erasure possible against an append-only ledger.
**One profile per guest** (ADAM CR-291, option B, decided 29 October 2026; CHG-R11GST-002): unique in the tenant, so `getMyProfile` and `updateMyProfile` read and write the one row of the session's subject. The profile's segment is the one it was first captured in.

preferredChannel.description: Left out where the guest has no preferred channel: a guest who chose `none` in `updateMyProfile` is stored as null and answered without this field (ADAM CR-291, option B; CHG-R11GST-002).

guestLinkId.description: Present where the guest is linked across cells. Marketing acts locally.

engagementScore.description:
22.2.20 and 22.2.21. **`lifetimeValue` and `visitCount` existed, so value was a stored figure and engagement was not.** They are different questions: a guest who spent a lot once and a guest who visits monthly have the same LTV and need opposite treatment.
**Recency, frequency and breadth, not spend** — spend is already `lifetimeValue`, and folding it in here would make one number twice.

engagementTier.description: 5.3.19. **Automatic classification, computed rather than assigned.** `lapsing` is the tier the whole field exists for — **a guest who has not been for a while and still might is the only one marketing can change**, and lumping them with `lapsed` wastes the window.

lifetimeValue.description: **Left out of guest reads until a guest's lifetime value has a currency** (ADAM CR-141, 18 October 2026; CHG-CRA-007): an amount above a venue is in the currency recorded on its own row (CR-094's rule, which waits on the client), and this row records none yet.

mergedIntoSubjectId.description: **Set on the absorbed profile by `mergeGuestProfiles` and `mergeGuests`**, which retain it as a redirect rather than deleting it. A read that lands here follows it; a second merge of a profile that has one is refused as `alreadyMerged`.

id.description: **Added 20 August.** The schema reference derives table columns from API response schemas, and a response is not a table — this one returned everything a caller needs and not the row's own identity, so the table had no key and no row could be addressed, updated or deleted. Found by an audit of all 365 tables, not by a reader.

GuestRelationship.description: Boards 1.7 and 1.8. **Links people without merging them**, which is the whole design.

authorities.description: **Four different permissions, not one relationship.** A guardianship granting all of them forever survives the child becoming an adult.

GuestTimelineEvent.description: Board 1.5. **Facts, notes and predictions distinguished on the row.**

nature.description: **A prediction and a gate scan are both useful and only one happened.**

IdentityGuestVerification.description: **One guest identity-document verification** (5.3.21; decided 29 September, build pass): the document it checks, its status, the method and who decided. The document itself is `pii.subject_document`; this row holds no document number.

documentImageDeletedAt.description: When the scan (and any selfie) was deleted under the policy's retention.

selfieUploadId.description: **The selfie sent with the document** (R8 blocker IDENTITY-C66, CHG-R8MIG-027): the `assets.guest_upload` id of the request's `selfieAssetId`, kept for the reviewer and deleted with the scan (`documentImageDeletedAt`, then null). Null when none was sent.

LoyaltyAdjustmentResult.x-ticvai-persistence: none — composed from the entry posted and the resulting position
LoyaltyAdjustmentResult.description: **Both halves of an adjustment, because returning only the balance is the defect decision 8 named.** Until 20 September this operation moved `marketing.loyalty_position` and returned it, and posted nothing to `marketing.loyalty_points` — so a manual adjustment was the one movement in the system that could not be walked back to a reason.

leaderboardNickname.description:
BL-173. **The name shown on a leaderboard, chosen by the guest.** Offered whenever they reach the board and changeable afterwards; `setLeaderboardNickname` is the only thing that writes it.
**Null means the guest has not chosen one yet, and the board shows a generated `Player-4821` in its place** — never `pii.subject.display_name`, which would disclose silently on the day a guest first placed and is the case this field exists to prevent.
**The generated name is computed at read time and not stored here.** Writing it would make *"has this guest chosen a name"* unanswerable, and that flag is what the prompt-on-reaching-the-board depends on.

tierId.description: **The tier this row's `tierCode` and `tierName` are a copy of.** Added 20 September with `marketing.programme_tier`: the two strings were a cache of something that did not exist, and a cache with no source cannot be rebuilt or audited.

MarketingGuestExtraField.description: **Taken from the backend workbook, 20 September.** NEW TABLE. Defines an extra field that Admin wants to add to the customer form, such as Date of Birth, Emergency Contact, or Jersey Size.

MarketingGuestExtraOption.description: **Taken from the backend workbook, 20 September.** NEW TABLE. Stores dropdown choices only when an extra field uses SELECT type, for example Language = English, Hindi, Marathi.

scopePath.description: Where the row is owned: the path of the scope that wrote it (its venue, or the region or tenant that configured it), set by the server from the caller's scope and never taken from a request. Row-level security reads it, so a venue writes and reads its own rows (MOD audit, 14 October 2026, CHG-MOD-007).

MarketingLoyaltyPoints.description: **Taken from the backend workbook, 20 September.** Stores every loyalty point earn, redeem, expire, adjustment, or reversal transaction for a customer.

scopePath.description: Where the row is owned: the path of the scope that wrote it (its venue, or the region or tenant that configured it), set by the server from the caller's scope and never taken from a request. Row-level security reads it, so a venue writes and reads its own rows (MOD audit, 14 October 2026, CHG-MOD-007).

reason.description: For a manual movement, `AdjustLoyaltyPointsRequest.reason`. Null for an accrual, a redemption or an expiry, whose `transactionType` and source already say why. The three manual types are the only ones (audit R149).

authorPrincipalId.description: Who posted a manual movement. Null where the platform posted it.

loyaltyPoints.description: The total points moved across every programme. The per-programme outcome is `loyaltyProgrammes`.

loyaltyProgrammes.description: **One entry per loyalty programme either record belonged to (decided 28 September, audit R149).** Points are added and the higher tier is kept, per programme — a single points number cannot say which programme it belongs to.

pointsAdded.description: The absorbed record's balance in this programme, added to the survivor's.

tierKept.description: The higher of the two records' tiers in this programme.

consentOutcome.description: Per purpose, the resulting position. Where the two profiles disagreed, the more restrictive position won.

channels.description: Omit to apply to every channel the purpose covers.
